shouldFix.title: ROLELESS-NA is introduced as the lawful alternative to a nonempty role set, but every downstream clause classifies an empty role set as REFUSE-only and no clause gives the sentinel a disposition or a domain-cell value
shouldFix.subjectEvidence: roleApplicability.rule offers two lawful states: 'Every comparison-basis component identity MUST have a nonempty applicable-role set drawn from the product-selected DR-118 list, OR an explicit ROLELESS-NA sentinel cell.' Every clause that then acts on the value collapses the second into the unlawful case. roleApplicability.completeness: 'Missing, EMPTY, conflicting, or out-of-list applicability is AMBIGUOUS-REFUSE-ONLY.' Step 3: '...or missing/EMPTY/conflicting/out-of-list roleApplicability' among the REFUSE-only conditions, with no ROLELESS-NA carve-out. roleApplicabilityBasis repeats both halves in one breath: 'MUST-nonempty ... or an explicit ROLELESS-NA sentinel cell. Missing/empty/conflicting/out-of-list applicability retains named cells and forces REFUSE/NON-PASS.' C-MISSING-ROLE-APPLICABILITY is defined as 'missing, empty, conflicting, or out-of-list roleApplicability' and G16-3 makes it refuse-only. Nothing anywhere states that ROLELESS-NA is not empty.
shouldFix.counterexample: A comparison-basis component identity to which no product-selected DR-118 role applies - the case the sentinel exists for - is recorded as ROLELESS-NA. Its applicable-role set is empty in fact. Step 3 matches 'empty roleApplicability' and classifies AMBIGUOUS-REFUSE-ONLY, so every change touching that identity emits a typed refusal and no lane ever runs. The sentinel the repair introduced as the lawful alternative is, as written, a permanent deadlock. Separately, fixtureDomainBasis.members builds cells from 'every product-selected DR-118 role applicable to that identity'; for a ROLELESS-NA identity that factor is empty, which is exactly the empty-factor omission MCICV7-B1 was raised about, and the only rule that retains cells - missingMetadata - retains them as C-MISSING-ROLE-APPLICABILITY cells, i.e. as the unlawful case again.
shouldFix.asymmetryWithTheSameCycle: This cycle solved the identical problem correctly one field away. The platform axis got a concrete sentinel VALUE for domain cells - 'platform=MISSING sentinel' - and DEF-WIN got an explicit disposition, DEFERRED-OUT-OF-PREVIEW-DOMAIN, spelled out as 'slot-complete and qualification-neutral. It is not blocked-on-ride, not INACTIVE, and not NON-PASS.' ROLELESS-NA received neither: no disposition, no cell value, no exemption from step 3. The template for the fix is already in the artifact.
shouldFix.impact: This is fail-closed, not fail-open - it over-refuses rather than under-selecting - so it is not a safety escape and not a blocker. But it makes MCICV7-B1's stated alternative inoperative, and it leaves the newest custodied input with two clauses in the same node that cannot both be satisfied for the state they jointly describe.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Give ROLELESS-NA the treatment DEF-WIN received: an explicit disposition stating it is slot-complete and qualification-neutral rather than an ambiguity, a named role-axis cell value for the domain (the analogue of platform=MISSING), and an exemption in step 3 so that a declared ROLELESS-NA is distinguished from an empty or withheld role set. Alternatively drop the sentinel from rule and roleApplicabilityBasis and require every comparison-basis identity to carry a nonempty role set - but then say so once, because the current text offers a state it then forbids. /selector and /g16Tests/corpus are both already rostered paths.

advisories.title: G16-14 reconciles against fixtureDomainBasis while coverageLaw's domain is fixtureDomainBasis plus deferredSlots
advisories.measurement: coverageLaw defines the closed domain as 'fixtureDomainBasis (pre-mutation) plus deferredSlots'. G16-14 requires that 'the executed cell set MUST reconcile exactly against the basis that digest commits to', and digestRule commits the digest to the basis alone. The two scopes differ by the deferred slots, so a run's deferred-slot cells are outside what G16-14 reconciles, and the word 'exactly' could be read as forbidding them as surplus.
advisories.whyAdvisoryOnly: No escape and no contradiction in practice. G16-14's enumerated failure modes are shortfall, post-mutation domain and omitted digest - surplus is not among them - and deferred-slot coverage is independently required by coverageLaw's omission clause and by G16-10. The risk is a harness author reading 'exactly' as an equality constraint and dropping DEF-WIN cells to satisfy it.
advisories.suggestedFix: Say that the executed set must reconcile against the basis plus the enumerated deferredSlots, or state that deferred-slot cells are outside the digest's commitment and covered by coverageLaw.

systemicObservation: Third consecutive candidate with no blocker, and the trend inside the findings is as informative as the count: v6 had two SHOULD-FIX in bookkeeping, v7 two in the newest repair, v8 two again in the newest repair, and each cycle's repairs are landing more completely than the last. Both surviving findings are the same species this chain keeps producing - a repair adds a member or a state, and one clause that enumerates or dispositions that kind of thing is not updated. V8-S1 is a new state (ROLELESS-NA) without the disposition treatment its sibling DEF-WIN received in the same cycle; V8-S2 is two new members without the ID-DEP-C6 enumeration that a prior blocker established as required when a member is added. The two authoring-time greps proposed at v5 and v7 would have caught V8-S2 directly - grep every clause that enumerates the ownership record's members, and ID-DEP-C6 returns a three-item list against authority's six. A third check would have caught V8-S1: when a repair introduces a named sentinel or exceptional state, grep for that token and confirm every clause that classifies the underlying value distinguishes it; 'ROLELESS-NA' appears twice and neither occurrence is in a classification clause. The substantive contract has now been stable for four generations.
verdictBasis: Zero blockers and two SHOULD-FIX findings; the dispatch admits ACCEPT only at zero and zero. All six claimed repairs are real and verified against the subject's bytes, and every predecessor verdict record is certified directly against frozen bytes. Both surviving findings were introduced by this cycle's MCICV7-B1 repair rather than carried, and neither is an under-selection escape - V8-S1 is fail-closed and V8-S2 is a ride-discipline omission with fully specified behaviour underneath it.
verdictStatement: v8 answers every finding from both v7 reviews and answers the two this reviewer raised at the level each was open. Missing platform metadata is now a step-3 REFUSE-only condition with a platform=MISSING sentinel and a place on the authority roster, so the oracle no longer demands a value the algorithm cannot emit. G16-14 makes the pre-mutation domain digest a required emission with exact reconciliation, closing the auditability gap in the anti-shrink law. Step 3 is declared the single enumeration of REFUSE-only conditions and the other three clauses now defer to it by reference. Role applicability becomes a custodied DR-118 component→role map that an empty factor cannot erase, DEF-WIN gets a lawful qualification-neutral disposition, and conflict-refuse is retired from the current enum while its v5 origin is kept on the record. The roster is closed at zero off-roster paths, and the D-111 HEAD move is confirmed append-only with file 08, the pinned sources and the subject all unmoved. What remains are two consequences of the newest repair. ROLELESS-NA is offered as the lawful alternative to a nonempty role set, yet step 3, the completeness rule, the change class and the corpus basis all classify an empty role set as REFUSE-only with no carve-out and no cell value - so a legitimately roleless identity refuses forever, and the sentinel is inoperative. And ID-DEP-C6 still enumerates three ownership-record members after two more were added, leaving the DR-118 role map - which the artifact states is explicitly not a DR-103 input - with no identity-dependency ride at all. DR-121 remains OPEN; DR-G16 remains PROPOSED, not QUALIFIED.
authorityOfThisVerdict: This verdict is a reviewer opinion recorded for coordinator disposition. It applies nothing, edits no subject, marks no row SATISFIED, marks no gate QUALIFIED, authorizes no implementation, chooses no CI vendor, mints no D-096 (A) grant, and does not touch docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md or docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. It did not edit the review prompt it was given.
coordinatorNote: A v9 needs one path that has never been rostered in this chain - /identityDependencies - plus /selector and /g16Tests/corpus, which are already rostered and carry the whole of V8-S1. No design work is outstanding for V8-S2; it is an enumeration and one ride declaration. V8-S1 does need a decision the coordinator should make rather than the author: whether a comparison-basis component identity with no applicable DR-118 role is a lawful preview state at all. If it is, ROLELESS-NA needs DEF-WIN's disposition treatment and a role-axis cell value; if it is not, the sentinel should be removed from rule and roleApplicabilityBasis and every identity required to carry a nonempty role set. The two answers differ on whether such a component can ever ship in the preview slice. Two process notes. First, the frozen-predecessor-readable convention has now paid off in four consecutive cycles and let this verdict certify all seven predecessor records; it is worth stating explicitly in future prompts. Second, if a v9 roster is drawn by asking 'which clauses enumerate a set this repair added to, and which clauses classify a state this repair named' rather than by listing the clauses the reviews cited, this chain reaches zero-zero.
